definition: Language resource management – Lexical markup framework (LMF; ISO 24613), produced by ISO/TC 37, is the ISO standard for natural language processing (NLP) and machine-readable dictionary (MRD) lexicons.
details: The scope is standardization of principles and methods relating to language resources in the contexts of multilingual communication.

explainer.lead: LMF is the ISO standard (ISO 24613) for representing NLP and machine-readable dictionary lexicons. It matters because it gives multilingual language resources a common structural footing.

tiers.eli5: It is a shared blueprint for lexicons, so a dictionary built by one team can be read and reused by another.
tiers.practitioner: Teams structure lexical data to conform to LMF so lexicons can be shared across tools and languages. A pitfall is that standard-conformant modelling adds structure that small projects may not need.
tiers.paperLevel: Produced by ISO/TC 37, it standardises principles and methods for language resources in multilingual communication contexts. It specifies structure, not the content of any particular lexicon.

explainer.example: A bilingual dictionary project stores its entries in an LMF-conformant structure so downstream NLP tools can consume them directly.
